definition.availability_rule: Use only observed closes at or before signal close t. Current historical download is not a vintage archive.
definition.execution_rule: No earlier than next observed close after t; last-row signal has no execution observation. No tradability or performance claim.
definition.hypothesis: Exploratory short-horizon close-momentum hypothesis on the frozen A-share convenience sample: keep the trailing five-observation close return and its direction, but divide it by trailing realized daily-return volatility over the same horizon, so each symbol's score is expressed in units of its own recent daily-return dispersion instead of a raw decimal return. Motivation is descriptive only: the frozen price profile records materially different one-observation return dispersion and extreme-return magnitudes across the three symbols, and baseline score dispersion tracks that contrast, so raw trailing returns sit on different scales across symbols, which may complicate later cross-symbol comparison. This is a proposal for later independent evaluation, not deployment: the rescaled score is unproven in sign and usefulness, is not an annual Sharpe ratio, and does not remove systematic risk or identify corporate actions. Timing follows the frozen source contract: calculations use only observed closes at or before the signal close, and any execution consideration is no earlier than the next observed close; counts of signals with a next observed close are availability counts only, not evidence of tradability, fills, costs or executable trades. Closes are unadjusted CNY per share; raw and normalized scores are both dimensionless.

inspection.limits: Descriptive scores only. No forward labels, PnL, alpha, formal evaluation or proof that a revision is better. Sample SD uses n-1; windows use past observed rows, with no filling. Historical price jumps cannot identify corporate actions.

limitations: Development sample only; this inspected data cannot become an untouched holdout.
An available next observed close does not establish tradability, fills or transaction costs.
Raw return and volatility-normalized return are both dimensionless; scaling changes magnitude, not units.
No forward labels, returns after execution, alpha, causality or superiority were measured.
Unadjusted historical closes are not vintage data or evidence of corporate actions.
The observed-date sample is neither an exchange calendar nor a representative market universe.
body.rationale: Decision: adopt the volatility-normalized alternative for exploratory research rather than retaining the raw baseline. Grounds: the recorded findings, supported by the frozen price profile, show materially different one-observation return dispersion and extreme-return magnitudes across the three symbols, and the baseline inspection's score dispersion tracks that contrast; scaling each symbol's trailing return by its own recent daily-return dispersion is a direct, schema-conforming exploratory response to that observed contrast. My receipt for this exact adopted specification establishes every descriptive consequence relied on here: required trailing closes per signal, warmup exclusions distinguished from additional exclusions, eligible signals, signals with a next observed close, per-symbol score moments, and changed rows versus the initial candidate. Compared with the baseline inspection, eligibility and exclusions are unchanged while every score row changes scale; raw and normalized scores are both dimensionless, so this is a magnitude change, not a unit change, and it cannot establish superiority, alpha, removal of systematic risk, improved comparability or corporate-action handling; the volatility-scaled score is not an annual Sharpe ratio. No return-magnitude bound was added because no cited evidence identifies observed extremes as data errors or corporate actions. Lack of proven alpha is a limitation for later independent evaluation, not a ground to reject exploration; retention was coherent but would leave the recorded dispersion observation unaddressed.

native_team_tasks.description: Analyze the operator baseline research candidate: five-observation raw close return, expression 1*(close[t]/close[t-5]-1), direction +1, no normalization, no volatility window, no return bound, on the frozen BaoStock sample (601318.XSHG, 600036.XSHG, 300750.XSHE; 62 common observed closes 2026-05-06..2026-07-31). Use only the frozen inline sources: research_contract, source_contract, data_quality, price_profile, and the three price series. Deliver structured findings that: (1) list applicability constraints directly supported by the sources (six trailing observations required before signal at close t; execution no earlier than the next observed close; last-row signal has no execution observation; no filling; observed union is not an exchange calendar; close-only jumps cannot identify corporate actions; current download not a vintage archive); (2) assess the observed price/return profiles, especially cross-symbol differences in one-observation return dispersion and extremes, and motivate at most one alternative specification strictly from the allowed FactorSpec schema (lookback 2..20, direction -1/+1, normalization none/realized_volatility with volatility_window 5..20 or null, max_absolute_daily_return 0..0.5 or null), stating expected coverage and score-scale consequences against the baseline and what evidence would be needed next; (3) keep every hypothesis explicitly unproven with no alpha, superiority, or backtest claims. Quote sources exactly where used. A coherent retention of the baseline is allowed.

native_team_tasks.description: Design the research candidate. Baseline is the frozen initial candidate: five-observation raw close return (lookback 5, direction 1, normalization none, volatility_window null, max_absolute_daily_return null). The single motivated alternative from finding:4 is lookback 5, direction 1, normalization realized_volatility, volatility_window 5, max_absolute_daily_return null. Steps: (1) run inspect_case_factor on the alternative spec exactly, and inspect the chosen final spec (baseline or alternative) before submission — use inspection_id/facts_sha256 references from your own receipts, never copied numbers; (2) compare coverage, exclusions and descriptive score-scale consequences against the baseline inspection (source:initial_inspection / inspection facts), citing finding:1, finding:2, finding:3, finding:4 where used; (3) explicitly decide to adopt the alternative for exploratory research or retain the baseline, with reasons grounded in the findings — descriptive score differences cannot establish superiority, no return bound may be added without cited evidence, a volatility-scaled score is not an annual Sharpe ratio, and lack of proven alpha is not grounds to reject exploration; (4) submit the exact final candidate via revise_case_factor per the structured-v3 contract (no digits in qualitative text or decision reasons; fact_refs for all numeric points; parent/decision basis from finding:N references). Keep every hypothesis unproven; no backtest, alpha, or superiority claims.
native_team_tasks.subject: author-2: design

native_team_tasks.description: Review the exact latest candidate version (the author-2 revision, candidate:2, spec lookback 5 / direction 1 / normalization realized_volatility / volatility_window 5 / max_absolute_daily_return null) and its complete structured report. Procedure: read the complete structured report (report pages via case_read, all pages concatenated) and the full candidate revision including decisions, count_claims, citations, hypothesis and rationale; bind report_sha256='assigned' from the report delivered to you. Check at minimum: (a) exact-version integrity — the reviewed candidate is the latest revision and its spec matches the recorded current spec; (b) semantic validity of the adoption decision and each disposition against finding:1, finding:2, finding:3, finding:4, including that the adopted alternative is the single motivated one and no extra parameter or return bound was added; (c) inspection binding — inspection_id and facts_sha256 refer to the author's own receipt for this exact spec, with coverage/exclusion claims consistent with recorded count facts; (d) contract compliance — no digits in qualitative hypothesis/rationale/decision text, fact_refs present for numeric points, no alpha, superiority, backtest, tradability or annual-Sharpe claims, timing/coverage constraints preserved (observations at/before t, next observed close, last-row no-execution, no filling, no corporate-action inference), and exploratory-unproven status explicit. Report checks as enums without restating computed values; an issue is a defect, not a disclosed caveat. Submit via review_case_factor per the structured-v3 contract; if defects exist, record them precisely for a possible repair.
